i just keep thinking about it... they said it has to align with doctrine and oversight. but feeding people and stopping evictions, isn't that already what jesus would be doing? like, what's more christ-like than that?

Yeah. Feeding people and keeping them from getting thrown out of their homes is not some side hobby Jesus would get around to after the doctrinal paperwork. That *is* the work. Hungry people, people with nowhere stable to sleep — that’s the center of the story, not a branding problem.

So when they said it had to “align with doctrine and oversight,” and the thing that didn’t align was you putting a mic in front of people actually doing that work… that’s a pretty hollow use of those words. Doctrine isn’t supposed to be a filter that screens out mercy unless it comes with a verse overlay. If the bar is “Jesus quote in every sentence,” that’s not discernment. That’s branding.

A couple things can be true at once, and I don’t want to pretend I can see into their heads:

They may sincerely believe a church platform can’t host groups that don’t share their theology, even if the work looks like the gospel. Some churches treat “feeding people” as okay and “organizing against evictions” as politics. That distinction is real in a lot of churches. It is also, a lot of the time, fear wearing a clerical collar — fear of looking “too political,” fear of who might get mad, fear of anything that isn’t already inside their language.

What *isn’t* shepherding is this: they pulled the series without talking to you first, told you after, and kept the reason from the congregation. That’s not careful oversight. That’s control plus secrecy. Shepherds don’t disappear someone’s work and then explain it in private so nobody else has to sit with the decision. That part is on them, and the humiliation you’re carrying is a reasonable response to being handled that way.

The people you interviewed feeding folks and fighting evictions — that work doesn’t get less Christ-like because it didn’t come with a proof text. You didn’t imagine that. You’re not crazy for noticing the gap between “what would Jesus do” and “take it down so it doesn’t make us nervous.”

I’m sorry they did it like that. You didn’t deserve to find out after the fact, and you didn’t deserve to be the only one who has to sit with why it vanished.
